svg.title: An Avro manifest stores each file entry as a row, with column statistics in maps over every column, so finding one column's bounds decodes every entry in full. A Parquet manifest stores each field as a column, so a filter on c2 reads only the path column and c2's typed statistics. Commits benefit too, since they read narrow slices such as paths, statuses and counts.
svg.text: Avro: one entry at a time
Parquet: one column at a time
and c2's typed bounds, nothing else
commits read narrow slices too: paths, statuses, counts

figure.figcaption: Same manifest, two layouts. Planning and commits both want a few columns of it, not all of it.
